newsitem.title: UK: Leading UK farmer sees no price upturn until 1997.
newsitem.headline: Leading UK farmer sees no price upturn until 1997.

text.p: Grain prices may begin to claw back recent losses in 1997 but any recovery is likely to be modest, the director of a leading UK farm group said on Monday.

"I don't see an immediate rise in prices...We still have an awful lot of grain to get rid of," said David Richardson, director of Sentry Farming Group Plc, adding prices may rise slightly in the New Year.

Speaking to Reuters on the sidelines of a conference on Risk Management in Agriculture, Richardson said world grain supply was still "extremely finely balanced" despite a recovery from the lowest level of stocks in 20 years last June. The sharp drop in world prices was an overreaction by traders to a situation in which supplies moved from being in great shortage to less great shortage in a relatively small period of time, he said.
In the European Union, prices were hammered by a record crop this year expected to reach up to 205 million tonnes while world demand for imports has slowed down.
On the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE), the benchmark November contract shed 20 percent since the peak in April, trading at 97.50 stg a tonne on Monday.

Richardson told conference delegates that in the medium to long term the world may be looking more at shortages of food than at surpluses because present farming methods were unlikely to satisfy the growing population.
"But that may be 10, 15 even 20 years away," he said. "In the meantime...the next few years are likely to be a bumpy ride."
